title: Unit tests for an ad campaign budget pacer
name: Budget pacer tests

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how these unit tests are designed to check the pacer's decisions? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is none. The current time is injected as a function and every test pins it to an explicit UTC instant, so results do not depend on when or in which timezone the suite runs. Boundaries are tested on both sides: 600_000 vs 600_001 at noon (target 500_000 plus 10% tolerance), and 999_000 vs 999_500 for the exhausted check with a 1_000 bid. The pacer holds no mutable state, so sharing `noon` across tests is safe.

choiceQuestions.prompt: At 12:00 UTC with a 1,000,000-micro daily budget and default tolerance, what is the largest spentTodayMicros that still gets reason "ok" (with a small bid that does not exhaust the budget)?
choiceQuestions.explanation: fractionOfDayElapsed is 0.5, so target is 500,000 and the ceiling adds 1,000,000 * 0.1 = 100,000, giving 600,000. The check is `spent > ceiling`, so exactly 600,000 is allowed, as the "exactly at the tolerance ceiling" test asserts. 500,000 is just the target, 550,000 has no basis in the code, and 1,000,000 ignores pacing.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why do the tests build times with explicit "Z" (UTC) ISO strings rather than local times?
choices: fractionOfDayElapsed uses getUTC* methods, so local-time inputs would give different fractions on machines in different timezones
Date cannot parse ISO strings without a timezone
It makes the tests run faster
choiceQuestions.explanation: The pacer computes start of day with getUTCFullYear/Month/Date. A date-time string without "Z" is parsed as local time, so on a CI machine in another timezone the UTC fraction would differ and the tests would be environment-dependent. Date parses such strings fine, the pacer has no rejection logic, and speed is unaffected.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Near the end of the day (23:59 UTC), spend is 999,500 and the bid is 1,000. Which check decides the outcome?
choices: Neither; the bid is allowed because the day is almost over
The tolerance check, which is skipped near midnight
The exhaustion check, returning exhausted, because it runs first
choiceQuestions.explanation: decide() first checks spent + bid > daily: 1,000,500 > 1,000,000, so it returns exhausted before computing the pacing target. At 23:59 the ceiling is above the budget, so pacing alone would not block. There is no midnight special case.
